title: Statistical Complexity of Soft Bellman Residual Minimization
claim: Empirical error measures decay at the predicted rate of roughly 1/n across data regimes, matching the exact empirical minimizer.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared legend below, grey slope-guide lines
description: Three log-log line plots sit side by side, each with n (about 10^2 to 10^4) on the x-axis. The panels show primal argument stability (parameters), function-space stability, and excess population MSBE. Each panel has colored curves with markers. Blue circles are H=8 i.i.d., orange squares are H=16 i.i.d., green triangles are H=32 i.i.d. A dashed orange line with hollow squares is a single trajectory at H=16. In the right panel a dotted dark line with x markers is the exact empirical minimizer. Two grey dashed reference lines labeled n^-1 and n^-1/2 give the slopes. All curves fall roughly parallel to the n^-1 guide. The curves nearly overlap, apart from the blue curve in the left panel, which sits higher. A single legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the steeply descending colored curves and the grey guides.
caption: \edit{Primal argument stability, function-space stability and excess population MSBE of the SGDA output against $n$ (log--log), averaged over 50 repetitions. Solid lines: i.i.d.\ data; dashed: a single trajectory; dotted: exact empirical minimizer. Grey guides show slopes $-1$ and $-1/2$.}
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning and offline inverse reinforcement learning aim to recover near-optimal value functions or reward models from a fixed batch of logged trajectories, yet current practice still struggles to enforce Bellman consistency scalably. Bellman residual minimization (BRM) has emerged as an attractive remedy. While globally convergent gradient-based soft (i.e., entropy-regularized) BRM methods for neural networks have recently been established, their statistical complexity under stochastic gradient descent remains largely unknown. In this paper, we address this theoretical gap for soft BRM. Through a Lyapunov-based analysis under a uniform PL condition in the auxiliary variable, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(1 / n)$ primal argument stability bound up to optimization error and an $\mathcal{O}(1 / n)$ statistical complexity for the soft BRM objective under the stated sampling conditions.
